items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a popular geography YouTube Shorts channel. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller: brisk and curious, with natural emphasis and a short comic pause before each punchline; quieter and serious for the line about the boy. Chars voices funny cartoon characters, short and punchy.
lines: Narrator
Under your feet here, a fire has burned for sixty-four years. Population: five. So why did nobody stop it?
Narrator
Rewind to nineteen sixty-two. Centralia, Pennsylvania. A coal town of about fourteen hundred people.
Narrator
The story goes, the town burned its trash in an old mining pit.
Narrator
But that pit sat on old coal mines. And the fire got in.
Chars
[cheeky, crackly, delighted little ember, fast and greedy] Ooh. Coal? For me?
Narrator
So they dug. They flushed. About forty-two thousand dollars later, the money ran out... The fire didn't.
Narrator
So how bad could it get?
Narrator
By nineteen seventy-nine, petrol in an underground tank hit seventy-eight degrees Celsius.
Chars
[grumpy old coal-town, sweaty and suspicious, slow] Is it just me... or the ground?
Narrator
In nineteen eighty-one, the ground opened under a twelve-year-old boy. A hole about forty-five metres deep.
Narrator
His cousin pulled him out. Now America was watching.
Narrator
Putting the fire out? One study said about six hundred and sixty-three million dollars.
Narrator
Moving everyone out? Forty-two million. Yes... that number again.
Narrator
So America didn't put out the fire... it put out the town.
Narrator
Over five hundred homes and shops were bought and torn down. In two thousand two, even the ZIP code went.
Narrator
Today, a handful of people still live there. Steam still rises through the cracks.
Narrator
And the twist? At this rate, it could burn for another two hundred and fifty years.
Chars
[cheeky, crackly, delighted little ember, fast and greedy] Relax. I'm only sixty-four.
Narrator
This is Bhoogol. Follow for more Geography Fun Facts.
